page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.18xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 72 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. It lacks simultaneous multithreading, providing exactly one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 576.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server is equipped with 45,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 112 Gbps. There are no GPUs present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional capabilities in memory and database operations. The instance achieves top-tier performance in memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block, read-only large block, and write large block metrics. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations and PassMark database tests, also rank in the top tier, alongside static web serving throughput. Multi-core compute performance is strong, as demonstrated by top-tier scores in Geekbench multi-core and software compilation with Clang, as well as strong results in multi-core stress-ng tests. Single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, falls into the average category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i8ge.18xlarge offers a highly dense storage and memory profile, making it a resource-dense option for large-scale deployments without the added cost of GPU hardware. However, a notable tradeoff is its single-core performance and certain single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression, which perform at average levels. Additionally, LLM text generation for very small models is poor, though text generation for medium and large models remains strong. This server is highly suited for high-throughput database systems, large-scale Redis deployments, static web serving, software compilation, and memory-intensive data processing workloads.
